summary: Streaming requests hang at high concurrency when tensor-parallel (TP) enabled (stuck streams / eventual client timeout)
description:
Customer reports intermittent hangs on streaming chat completions under high concurrency with tensor-parallel enabled. Symptoms: client receives initial tokens, then stream stalls indefinitely (no further chunks) until client-side timeout (typically 120–180s). When stalls occur, Dedicated capacity shows rising queue depth and increased tail latency; some requests never complete and require manual worker recycle.

Issue Summary
- What: Streaming requests stall (no forward progress) under sustained load, only when TP enabled.
- Where: Dedicated cluster in eu-west.
- Impact: Elevated timeouts for end users, degraded throughput, oncall intervention to restore capacity.
- Frequency: 1–3 times/day during peak load windows; more likely with long-running streams.

Customer-provided details
- Workload: chat completions with streaming=true; mix of short (<=256 output tokens) and long (2k–4k output tokens) generations.
- Concurrency: ~400–700 concurrent streams.
- TP config: TP=4 on 4xH100 nodes (single host TP groups) + autoscaling; pinned runtime version 1.18.3.
- Mitigations tried by customer: reduced max_tokens and client timeout; did not eliminate stalls.

Initial hypothesis (based on recent patterns)
- TP group enters stuck state due to cancellation/barrier interaction during streaming disconnects or timeouts OR NCCL async error not surfacing promptly, leading to collectives waiting indefinitely.

Requested from customer
- 2 representative request_ids that stalled + approximate timestamps (UTC)
- confirmation whether client disconnects / retries during stall
- whether stalls correlate with autoscaling events or pod/worker restarts

Support actions
- Coordinated with Runtime Scheduling + Collectives to review logs/metrics, compare to known hang signatures, and propose hotfix/flags.

Attachments/links
- Customer shared: request logs (redacted), timestamps, and a HAR-equivalent trace for stalled streaming session (see comments).

resolution:
Resolved via Dedicated patch rollout to runtime 1.19.0-rc3 with TP cancellation/barrier deadlock fix and TP-group watchdog/quarantine enabled (opt-in). Customer confirmed no recurrence over 10-day window under peak concurrency.

Key changes associated with fix:
- Cancellation-safe barrier handling to prevent TP group deadlock during streaming disconnects/timeouts (redwood/pr-18441)
- Improved collective async error checks/failure propagation (redwood/pr-18455)
- TP-group forward-progress watchdog + quarantine/controlled teardown (redwood/pr-18462)
- Config knobs for collective timeout and watchdog thresholds (redwood/pr-18473)

Workarounds (prior to patch) that reduced impact:
- Cap concurrent streams, increase client/gateway idle timeouts, reduce aggressive retries during stall conditions.

Next steps
- Productized docs for recommended thresholds per deployment mode and streaming-heavy workloads.
- Ensure alerting/runbook coverage for stuck TP groups (INT-611).
